description: How the host cell or host immune system responds to the parasite or protein.
What is observed when the gene is perturbed -- imaging, drug sensitivity, differentiation.
What the protein is held to DO: GO terms, EC numbers, coarse functional class.
Which other molecules it is physically with.
Where in the cell, or at which interface, the protein is -- localisation knowledge.
Which covalent modifications the molecule carries (PTM sites, m6A).
How much of the protein there is.
What the primary sequence is and what can be read directly off it.
How much the parasite needs the gene to survive or grow in some condition.
What the folded shape is, and how confidently it is known.
How much of that RNA is being translated -- ribosome occupancy and efficiency.
The state of the locus itself: accessibility, histone marks, factor occupancy.
How much RNA of the gene there is, in some state or contrast.
